speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) what is the current percentage of full-time ITE students being able to secure internships and part-time jobs to add value to their training throughout their course; (b) how does ITE's Career Services Centre help place ITE students in internships; (c) what measures are in place to expand internship opportunities for ITE students; and (d) how many ITE graduates eventually work in the industries that they have been trained for.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: This means that more than half of the full-time students now enrolled in ITE would have done an internship by the time they graduate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Given the vocational nature of ITE courses, hands-on training is already an integral part of the curriculum for its students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Students may take up internships to reinforce their learning in the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: ITE matches students’ internships to internship places based on factors, such as their course of study, interests and also where they stay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: ITE has a dedicated team that will continue to engage its industry partners and trade associations to expand internship opportunities for its students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: It will also raise the quality of internships and make it a meaningful experience for students by introducing structured mentorships, defining learning outcomes and jointly conducting performance management with the industry partners.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Beyond training targeted at entry into specific industries or even related jobs, ITE graduates are also equipped with the skills that are transferrable across industries and sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: This gives them greater adaptability as the national manpower needs shift due to technological change and economic restructuring.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have two supplementary questions, two quick ones.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first one is with regard to the internship statistics that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary shared earlier.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary explain whether there is any differentiation between the traineeship programme that is being done in ITE where employers wish to send their employees to ITE and sort of fund them?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Is it separate from the internship statistics that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary shared earlier?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: When the Member asked about trainees sent by corporations to ITE, this is in appreciation by the employers that ITE's training is vocational by nature.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member is really asking about companies sending their workers to go to ITE for training, maybe at night or part-time learning, and so that is a separate programme viz-a-viz sending ITE students to companies.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, if the Member could file a separate Parliamentary Question (PQ), we will be very happy to provide more information on that component.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Every ITE and polytechnic campus is assigned six ECG counsellors and the remaining counsellors are assigned to secondary schools where four secondary schools will be looked after by one counsellor.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: These counsellors are recruited based on key considerations, such as their experience in the sector, and many of them would have very rich experience in industry.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Having said that, we pay a lot of attention to their professional development, which is why, every month, we will arrange for the ECG counsellors to attend briefings and training, not just classroom training but also field trips to the various industries, like Jurong Island or even LaunchPad@Jurong.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is important that they have insights into the latest labour market information and also understand the key industry trends, as well as the developments in the 23 Industry Transformation Maps.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In the school, the ECG counsellors, for example, ITE will work very closely with the lecturers ‒ actually they are called class coaches ‒ and arrange for the ECG counsellors to have coaching sessions with the class, as well as one-on-one sessions, if the students need.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Other than the ECG counsellors ‒ because every campus is assigned six counsellors ‒ in order for students to really understand the benefits of internship, the lecturers play an important role.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And this is why in the ITE we pay a lot of attention to pre-internship briefings for students to set the right expectations, share common expectations and also guidelines of the internship arrangement.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Even during the internship, ITE lecturers will pay regular visits to the students to make sure that the learning outcomes are fulfilled.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And after the internship, we will conduct feedback surveys to understand if their experience has fulfilled the learning objectives that were outlined before the internship.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Through our surveys, we may cease partnership with partnership companies that have breached the terms of the internship partnership agreement or have consistently received poor student outcomes.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the welfare, the learning outcome of the student, are at the heart of our ITE internship programme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can the Ministry share if it intends to increase the number of ECGs in the ITEs from the six currently?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I see the importance of internship for the ITE students, especially as it helps them to go into the industry as well.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The ECG initiative is about two years old and we are looking at it very closely in terms of how it has helped our students better understand how they can navigate and also make an informed decision for their education and career pathways.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Other than the one-on-one coaching with the students, where the ECG counsellors can also make a good impact is sharing the philosophy of what pedagogies are with the lecturers and the class coach, so that they can also impart and facilitate these decision makings by the students accordingly.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I must add that other than the ECG counsellors, the companies play an important role.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I have a supplementary question for the hon Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: It is good to know that there are internship programmes at the ITE.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: It is good to know that there are also target objectives for the institution.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: But I would like to know whether these targets have been deployed and brought down to the lecturers.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Are these lecturers also being measured on whether they have done the internship programmes correctly on them?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will review all feedback and I want to assure the Member that lecturers play a key role.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But this is not the only thing that the lecturers are doing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: They are also teaching the students the curriculum and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, if the Member has a particular question about key performance indicators for lecturers, he may wish to file a separate PQ and we will be very happy to provide more detailed information.
